newsitem.title: UK: SFO says Forsyth ruling doesn't change Nadir case.
newsitem.headline: SFO says Forsyth ruling doesn't change Nadir case.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Monday that the quashing of convictions against Elizabeth Forsyth, a former aide to Polly Peck head Asil Nadir, did not affect its case against Nadir.

"He (Nadir) remains a fugitive from justice and a warrant for his arrest is outstanding," the SFO said in a statement after Forsyth's two convictions for handling stolen cash were found to be unsafe because the appeal court said the trial judge had misdirected the jury.
Earlier, Nadir's lawyer Peter Krivinskas, who also represented Forsyth, told Reuters that Nadir would shortly begin a legal process aimed at paving the way for his return to Britain.

"I think he will shortly instruct me on his abuse of process application," Krivinskas said, adding that Nadir would not come back before a decision on this was given. Nadir, who skipped bail in 1993, faces charges connecting to his collapsed Polly Peck empire.
Forsyth, 60, spent 10 months in jail after she was found guilty of dishonestly handling 400,000 stg in April last year. Her sentence of five-years in jail was quashed in January.
The outcome of Forsyth's case was widely viewed as an indicator of whether Nadir would would press ahead with attempts to have theft and false accounting charges against him dropped.
Polly Peck, Nadir's fruit-to-electronics empire, collapsed in 1990 under a mountain of debt.
